aa_12_steps.title: Alcoholics Anonymous 12 Steps
aa_12_steps.description: Sequential recovery program combining personal accountability, spiritual awakening, and service
aa_12_steps.author: Alcoholics Anonymous

aa_12_traditions.title: Alcoholics Anonymous 12 Traditions
aa_12_traditions.description: Organizational and relational principles for AA groups and the fellowship
aa_12_traditions.author: Alcoholics Anonymous

hawkins_map.title: Hawkins Map of Consciousness
hawkins_map.description: 17-level hierarchical scale of human consciousness levels, calibrated from 0-1000, with emotional, physiological, and spiritual correlates
hawkins_map.source: Power vs. Force, David R. Hawkins
hawkins_map.author: David R. Hawkins

words_of_jesus.title: Words of Jesus (Gospel Discourses)
words_of_jesus.description: Major teachings and discourses of Jesus organized by thematic discourse blocks with translation variants
words_of_jesus.source: Gospel accounts (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John) - Multiple translations (KJV, RSV, ESV)
words_of_jesus.author: Jesus Christ (recorded by Gospel authors)
words_of_jesus.note: Organized by major discourse units; each includes multiple translation variants to show how different renderings affect meaning

discourse_01.title: The Beatitudes
discourse_01.content_summary: Blessings pronounced on those who embody spiritual poverty, mourning, meekness, hunger for righteousness, mercy, purity, peacemaking, and perseverance under persecution

application.practice: Contemplative reflection on spiritual poverty and receptiveness

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Willingness, healing; shift from powerlessness to possibility
External poverty as precondition for inner virtue

interpretation_layers.text: Direct proclamation of nine blessings (or eight in Luke); external conditions paired with internal spiritual qualities
Reversal of worldly values: blessed are those considered unfortunate or powerless (poor, mourning, meek)
Blessedness independent of external circumstances; joy found in alignment with God's kingdom values

translation_variants.verse_1: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven
Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God

applications: Identify which beatitude resonates most deeply
Examine how each beatitude inverts worldly values
Contemplate spiritual poverty as openness to divine grace
Practice mercy, peacemaking, and righteousness pursuit

discourse_02.title: Sermon on the Mount (Extended Teaching)
discourse_02.content_summary: Extended ethical teaching covering law fulfillment, anger, adultery, divorce, oaths, retaliation, love of enemies, prayer, fasting, wealth, worry, and judgment

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Cultivating inner character regardless of external circumstance
Love and acceptance as foundation for ethics

key_teachings: Fulfill the law by internalized righteousness, not external compliance
Anger toward brother as serious as murder; reconciliation paramount
Lust in heart equivalent to adultery; purity of intention matters
Love enemies; pray for persecutors; go second mile
Secret prayer more valuable than public display
Trust in Father's provision; seek kingdom first, all else added
famous_passages: Let your yes be yes and your no be no
Do to others as you would have them do to you
applications: Examine internal motivations, not just external actions
Practice forgiveness and reconciliation before making offerings
Cultivate purity of heart
Love actively including enemies
Trust in divine provision over anxious striving

discourse_03.title: The Lord's Prayer
discourse_03.content_summary: Model prayer teaching proper address to God, petition for kingdom manifestation, basic needs, forgiveness, guidance away from temptation, and deliverance from evil

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Prayer and meditation for conscious contact with Higher Power
Contemplative practice leading to wisdom and alignment

structure: Address: 'Our Father in heaven' — intimate relationship, shared belonging
Hallowing: 'Hallowed be your name' — reverence for divine reality
Kingdom: 'Your kingdom come, your will be done' — alignment with divine purpose
Provision: 'Give us our daily bread' — trust in sufficiency
Forgiveness: 'Forgive us as we forgive' — mutual release, reconciliation
Protection: 'Lead us not into temptation, deliver us from evil' — guidance and protection

translation_comparison.matthew_kjv: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name
translation_comparison.matthew_rsv: Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name

interpretations.text: Direct requests for God's kingdom, daily provision, forgiveness, protection
Meditation on God's nature, will, and relationship to human needs
Alignment of human will with divine will through prayer practice

applications: Pray daily using this model
Contemplate each petition's meaning
Connect forgiveness given with forgiveness received
Trust in provision while working
Recognize human limitations and need for guidance

discourse_04.title: The Parables of the Kingdom
discourse_04.content_summary: Teaching through parables about kingdom growth: sower, weeds, mustard seed, leaven, hidden treasure, pearl, fishing net. Emphasizes gradual growth, mixture of good and bad, and kingdom value

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Kingdom grows naturally like seed; cannot be forced
Willingness and growth orientation; trust in process

parables.meaning: Word of kingdom falls on different soil (hearts); only some bear fruit
parables.spiritual_lesson: Receptivity of heart determines fruitfulness; seed is sown regardless

parables.meaning: Good and evil coexist in kingdom; separation comes at harvest
parables.spiritual_lesson: Judgment deferred; patience with mixed community; God knows the tares

parables.meaning: Tiny beginning grows into large plant
parables.spiritual_lesson: Kingdom begins small but grows exponentially; organic development

parables.meaning: Kingdom worth any price; supreme value
parables.spiritual_lesson: Recognition of kingdom leads to joyful sacrifice of lesser goods

deep_dive.teaching_method: Jesus teaches in parables so hearers must actively interpret; understanding requires receptivity

discourse_05.title: I Am Statements (Johannine Self-Disclosure)
discourse_05.content_summary: Metaphorical self-identifications: I am the Bread of Life, Light of the World, Door, Good Shepherd, Resurrection and Life, Way Truth Life, True Vine. Each reveals aspect of Jesus's role and relationship to believers

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: God-consciousness; identity with divine
Union with universal Reason/Logos

i_am_statements.statement: I am the Bread of Life (John 6:35)
i_am_statements.meaning: Jesus sustains spiritual/eternal life; to consume him (believe/follow) is to live
i_am_statements.depth: Metaphor bridges material (hunger for food) and spiritual (hunger for meaning/life)

i_am_statements.statement: I am the Light of the World (John 8:12)
i_am_statements.meaning: Jesus illuminates truth, dispels darkness/ignorance/sin, guides followers
i_am_statements.depth: Light as fundamental metaphor for revelation, consciousness, divine presence

i_am_statements.meaning: Jesus is the entry point to salvation, kingdom, spiritual life
i_am_statements.depth: Access to divine reality mediated through relationship with Jesus

i_am_statements.meaning: Jesus cares for followers, guides, protects, knows them by name, lays down life
i_am_statements.depth: Shepherd metaphor invokes Psalm 23, divine care and protection; covenant relationship

i_am_statements.statement: I am the Resurrection and the Life (John 11:25)
i_am_statements.meaning: Jesus embodies and grants eternal life; death is not final
i_am_statements.depth: Present reality (I am) and future destiny (resurrection) unified in Jesus

i_am_statements.statement: I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life (John 14:6)
i_am_statements.meaning: Jesus is the path, the reality, and the life itself; access to Father through him
i_am_statements.depth: Trinity of relationship (way to Father), ontology (truth), and vitality (life)

i_am_statements.meaning: Jesus is source; followers are branches; fruitfulness through abiding in him
i_am_statements.depth: Organic connection; life flows from vine to branches; severance means death

deep_dive.theological_significance: I am (ego eimi) echoes divine name from Exodus ('I AM'); Jesus claims divine identity
applications: Contemplate how each statement illuminates an aspect of divine provision/relationship
Recognize human hunger (for food, truth, guidance, protection, life, meaning) as invitation to seek Jesus
Abide/remain in connection with Jesus as sustaining reality

discourse_06.title: Teaching on Love and Forgiveness
discourse_06.content_summary: Commands to forgive without limit (70 times 7), parables of lost sheep/coin/prodigal son showing God's relentless love for the lost, new commandment to love as Jesus loved

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Making amends; forgiveness of self and others
Unconditional acceptance and forgiveness
Compassion for human weakness

central_teachings: Forgive not seven times but seventy times seven (unlimited, boundless forgiveness)
Parable of Unforgiving Servant: shows consequences of withholding forgiveness
Parable of Lost Sheep: God rejoices more in finding one lost than keeping ninety-nine safe
Parable of Prodigal Son: Father runs to embrace returning son; feast of celebration
New Commandment: Love one another as Jesus loved (self-sacrificial)
Greatest Commandment: Love God, love neighbor as self
deep_dive.grace_emphasis: Forgiveness precedes repentance; love initiates reconciliation; God's generosity exceeds human expectation
deep_dive.transformation_metaphor: Lost things (sheep, coin, son) are found and restored; death and resurrection imagery throughout
applications: Practice unlimited forgiveness; release resentment
Recognize your own lostness and Father's pursuit
Celebrate others' return/restoration
Love actively, sacrificially, without condition
Extend same mercy received

discourse_07.title: Teaching on Hypocrisy and Judgment
discourse_07.content_summary: Warnings against pharisaic hypocrisy (outward righteousness masking inner corruption), instruction to judge oneself before judging others, parable of splinter and log

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Examine own vice before judging others' virtue
Willingness to see own complicity and error

warnings_against: Outward show (phylacteries, long prayers) without inner substance
Tithing herbs but neglecting justice, mercy, faithfulness
Cleaning outside of cup while inside remains full of greed and excess
Whitewashed tombs: beautiful outside but full of bones and decay inside
instruction_on_judgment: Do not judge, or you too will be judged
You will be judged by the standard you use to judge others
Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother's eye... while the plank is in your own?
First remove the plank from your eye, then you can see clearly to remove the speck
deep_dive.core_principle: Hypocrisy is claiming righteousness externally while remaining corrupt internally. Judgment begins with self-examination.
applications: Examine own hypocrisy before criticizing others
Align inner reality with outer profession
Release judgment stance; focus on own transformation
Recognize that judging others reflects unexamined corruption in self

discourse_08.title: Teaching on Money and Possessions
discourse_08.content_summary: Warnings about wealth as spiritual obstacle (easier for camel through needle's eye), teaching that life doesn't consist of possessions, cannot serve two masters (God and money), parable of rich fool

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Wealth and poverty as externals; focus on inner character
Detachment from outcomes; nonattachment to possessions

key_sayings: It is more blessed to give than to receive
No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and money
Watch out! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed
Life is not a matter of how much you own
Seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you
It is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom of heaven; easier for camel through needle's eye

parable_of_rich_fool.story: Man harvests abundant crops, plans larger barns for security/comfort, but dies that night
parable_of_rich_fool.meaning: Trust in possessions is false security; death renders possessions meaningless; spiritual poverty is the real lack

attitudes_toward_wealth: Wealth as spiritual obstacle: it can choke out kingdom-seeking
Possessions as test of allegiance: choosing kingdom over security
Generosity as spiritual practice: giving breaks grip of greed
Trust in provision: God cares for lilies and birds; how much more humans?
applications: Examine relationship to money; what does it reveal about trust?
Practice generosity as spiritual discipline
Seek kingdom first; trust provision will follow
Recognize that security in possessions is illusion

discourse_09.title: Teaching on Faith and Trust
discourse_09.content_summary: Commands to have faith like a mustard seed (can move mountains), teaching that whatever you believe you will receive when you pray, do not worry about tomorrow, illustrations of God's care for nature

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Belief that power greater than self can restore to sanity
Seeking through prayer to improve conscious contact
Willingness and trust; openness to possibility

core_teachings: Have faith in God / faith like mustard seed can move mountains
Whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it
Do not worry about tomorrow; sufficient unto the day is its own trouble
Look at birds: they don't sow, reap, or store; Father feeds them; you're worth more
Consider lilies: don't work or spin, yet Solomon in all glory not dressed like these
First seek kingdom and righteousness; all things will be added

faith_dynamics.belief_precedes_reception: Believe you receive it, then you shall have it; expectation aligns with manifestation
faith_dynamics.impossibility_overcome: What is impossible with humans is possible with God; faith bridges gap
faith_dynamics.trust_in_provision: Nature (birds, lilies) thrives without anxiety; humans can trust similarly

deep_dive.paradox: Ask believing you already have it; seek kingdom while trusting provision; act and surrender simultaneously
applications: Cultivate faith through practice; notice what you believe about yourself/God
Pray with confidence; claim what you ask in prayer
Release worry; notice how it blocks faith
Observe nature's provision; use it as mirror of divine care
Practice asking, believing, receiving

discourse_10.title: Farewell Discourse (Johannine)
discourse_10.content_summary: Last teachings before crucifixion: preparation of place in Father's house, promise of Holy Spirit as Advocate, abiding in Jesus as branches in vine, sending disciples into world as Jesus was sent, high priestly prayer for disciples

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Carrying message to others; commissioning of disciples
Love and intercession; unity consciousness

major_elements: Do not let your hearts be troubled; believe in God, believe in me
In my Father's house are many rooms; going to prepare place
I am the way, the truth, the life; no one comes to Father except through me
Those who have faith in me will do greater works than these
I will ask Father to send Holy Spirit/Paraclete/Advocate to be with you forever
Abide in me as branches abide in vine; apart from me you can do nothing
I am sending you as Father sent me into the world
High priestly prayer: Father, sanctify them in truth; make them one as we are one; give them glory
deep_dive.theological_depth: Ultimate revelation of Jesus's relationship to Father and disciples; promise of continued presence through Spirit; commissioning of mission
applications: Trust in Jesus's preparation of place; faith in resurrection/afterlife
Receive Holy Spirit as guide, teacher, comforter
Maintain connection through abiding/remaining in relationship
Accept commission to continue Jesus's mission in the world
Seek unity as reflection of Father-Son unity

discourse_11.title: Teaching on End Times and Judgment
discourse_11.content_summary: Olivet Discourse on temple destruction, signs of end times, parable of ten virgins (readiness), parable of talents (stewardship), judgment of nations (separating sheep from goats by how they treated the needy)

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Judgment; consequences of choices
How one lives determines destiny

parables.meaning: Five wise (prepared with oil), five foolish (unprepared); readiness for unexpected timing; preparation is daily practice
parables.application: Maintain alertness and readiness; don't assume you know the timing

parables.meaning: Master gives talents (wealth/gifts) to servants according to ability; expects return on investment; faithful stewardship rewarded, fearful hoarding punished
parables.application: Use gifts/resources actively; growth comes from risk; fear leads to stagnation

parables.meaning: Final judgment: righteous treated hungry/thirsty/stranger/sick/prisoner with love; unrighteous didn't; what you do for least you do for Jesus
parables.application: Love expressed through practical care for vulnerable is the ultimate measure; compassion is faith lived

key_teachings: Be alert, watching for signs; no one knows the day or hour
Many will come in my name saying 'I am'; do not be deceived
Gospel will be preached to all nations, then end will come
Judgment based on response to Jesus and care for the vulnerable

discourse_12.title: Resurrection Appearances and Commission
discourse_12.content_summary: Post-resurrection teachings: Great Commission to make disciples of all nations, promise of Jesus's presence and power, reception of Holy Spirit, authority given to disciples

parallels_in_other_systems.reason: Carrying message to others as primary spiritual purpose

core_commission: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me
Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them, teaching them to obey all I commanded
Surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age
You will receive power when Holy Spirit comes on you; you will be witnesses
As the Father sent me, I am sending you
grounding_promises: Holy Spirit will guide you into all truth (John)
Authority to forgive sins is given to you (John)
What you do in my name will be done (Mark)
deep_dive.transformation_note: Resurrection reverses crucifixion; death is not final; disciples' fear transforms to boldness through Spirit
applications: Accept commission to continue Jesus's teaching and witness
Trust Jesus's presence and Spirit's power for the work
Teach others to follow Jesus and obey his commands
Recognize authority given for spiritual work
Move from fear (pre-resurrection) to boldness (post-resurrection)
